STEP 1 - Scene: This is a snack or breakfast plate with two granola bars and a piece of baguette-style bread.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white dinner plate with ridged rims, about 27 cm across. Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Crunchy oat granola bar (oats and honey type)
- Chewy granola bar with chocolate chips and nuts
- Piece of French bread / baguette

STEP 4 - Area: Food covers about 22% of the plate.
- Oat bar: ~8% ≈ 46 cm²
- Chocolate chip bar: ~5% ≈ 29 cm²
- Bread: ~9% ≈ 51 cm²

STEP 5 - Volume (area × height):
- Oat bar: 46 × 1.0 = 46 ml
- Chocolate chip bar: 29 × 1.2 = 35 ml
- Bread: 51 × 5 = 255 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (volume × bulk density):
- Oat bar: 46 × 0.9 ≈ 41 g. A standard bar is about 21 g each, so this may be two stacked; I'll use ~40 g.
- Chocolate chip bar: 35 × 0.7 ≈ 25 g
- Bread: 255 × 0.28 ≈ 70 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Oat bar: 40 g × 470 kcal/100g = 188 kcal
- Chocolate chip bar: 25 g × 430 kcal/100g = 108 kcal
- Bread: 70 g × 270 kcal/100g = 189 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The total is about 135 g and 485 kcal. That is plausible for two snack bars and a piece of baguette.
